clue.text: Where Luther spoke for the early bird?

blocks.note: first meaning: the imperial assembly held at the German city of Worms in 1521, where Martin Luther defended his writings
second meaning: what the early bird eats, read literally as a menu of earthworms

explanation.surface: Martin Luther preaching a sermon to the birds at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says the early bird catches the worm, so its daily fare is literally a diet of worms; the historic Diet was an assembly, not a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A diet is a formal parliament of the Holy Roman Empire, and Worms is the Rhineland city where Luther was tried for heresy.

clue.text: Runners with their future detailed

blocks.note: surface reading: athletes whose prospects have been spelled out in detail
setter's reading: de-tailed, having their tails cut off, as happens to the nursery-rhyme runners who chased the farmer's wife

explanation.surface: Racers whose coming careers have been mapped out carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme the creatures all ran after the farmer's wife, who cut off their tails with a carving knife: so their fate was to be de-tailed.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme's three rodents are runners whose destiny, losing their tails to a carving knife, is foretold in the song.

clue.text: Piece taken from river in bar

indicators.note: one thing placed in another means the first sits inside the second

blocks.note: R is the standard abbreviation for river
bar as a preposition means apart from

explanation.surface: Someone fishing a chunk of something out of a river and into a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a pub or a rod, but it is the preposition, as in 'all bar one'.
explanation.definitionFit: An extract or passage lifted out of a longer text or film is a section removed from the whole work.

clue.text: For the theoretician the bad loo guide has a point

indicators.note: something bad is faulty or spoiled, so these letters are in a wrong arrangement to be fixed

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
a point of the compass: E for east

explanation.surface: A thinker remarks that a poor guide to public toilets still makes a fair point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has a point' reads as conceding an argument, but the point is a compass direction added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideologue is someone devoted to a theory or doctrine, often dogmatically, so a theorist of political ideas.

clue.text: Mythological work by youth leader on the Goon show

indicators.note: a show is a performance or display, so the letters are put on stage in a fresh arrangement
a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter of the word is taken

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the opening letter of youth

explanation.surface: A myth-based piece by a youth-club leader staged on The Goon Show, the 1950s BBC radio comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Goon Show was a surreal BBC radio comedy; here 'show' is a verb asking for the letters to be displayed in a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesiod's Theogony is an ancient Greek poem telling the genealogy and birth of the gods.

clue.text: Running properly, I get a Beatle to call New York wrongly when embraced by Polly

indicators.note: done wrongly means set out in the wrong order, so the letters must be rearranged
being embraced means being held in someone's arms, so these pieces go inside the outer word

blocks.note: taken as written
Ringo Starr, the Beatles' drummer
call as written plus NY, the abbreviation for New York
Little Polly Flinders, the nursery-rhyme girl who sat among the cinders

explanation.surface: A Beatles fan gets a Beatle to phone New York and is hugged by someone called Polly.
explanation.walkthrough: Polly needs her surname from the nursery rhyme; everything else sits between its first letter and the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine with every cylinder igniting fuel is working at full power, so the idiom means functioning at its best.

clue.text: See 5
Scottish king of military rank drowned in a lot of wine

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the word loses its ending
something drowned in liquid is submerged and surrounded by it, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: COL is the abbreviation for colonel
Malmsey is a sweet Madeira wine

explanation.surface: A Scottish king of high military rank drowned in a vat of wine, as the Duke of Clarence was said to be.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first four letters of the wine are used; the rank goes inside them. Clarence, in Shakespeare's Richard III, was drowned in a butt of Malmsey.
explanation.definitionFit: Malcolm was the name of several medieval kings of Scotland, including the Malcolm who defeats Macbeth.

clue.text: Dairy product, a cat and mouse affair?

blocks.note: the grinning Cheshire Cat of Alice in Wonderland
the food mice are traditionally said to love

explanation.surface: A cat-and-mouse chase over a dairy food.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheshire is an English county famous for its crumbly cheese, and its cat grins in Alice in Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheshire is one of England's oldest named cheeses, a crumbly hard variety made from cow's milk.

clue.text: Noisy or sporty criminal?

blocks.note: surface reading: a lawbreaker who is either loud or keen on games
setter's reading: a racket is a din and also a bat for tennis, so the crook's title seems to come from either

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a crook is loud or athletic.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for this crook looks built from a din or a tennis bat, though it actually comes from a racket meaning a fraudulent scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A racketeer is someone who runs a dishonest money-making scheme such as extortion or protection, so a criminal.

clue.text: God gives every satisfaction

blocks.note: every and all both mean the whole lot
a sigh of satisfaction

explanation.surface: A believer's claim that God provides complete contentment.
explanation.definitionFit: Allah is the Arabic name for the one deity of Islam, used also by Arabic-speaking Christians.

clue.text: Put down Scottish region when returning

indicators.note: returning means going back the way you came, so the word is read from end to start

blocks.note: Lorne, or Lorn, is a district of Argyll in western Scotland

explanation.surface: Someone disparaging a Scottish area when they come back from it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put down' suggests belittling, but here it means writing a name on a list.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol someone is to enter their name on a register, so to write them down for a course or roll.

clue.text: Nerve centres of a group with pride?

blocks.note: a gang is a group of people
a pride is the collective noun for lions

explanation.surface: Asking whether a proud group of people has nerve centres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pride' reads as self-esteem, but it is the collective noun for big cats.
explanation.definitionFit: A ganglion is a cluster of nerve cell bodies acting as a relay point in the nervous system.

clue.text: One going to court and t-tailing off

indicators.note: off means gone bad or not right, so the letters are out of their proper order

blocks.note: taken as written, stammer and all

explanation.surface: Someone heading to court, stammering as their voice trails away.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter looks like decoration but supplies an extra letter; 'off' means the letters go off in a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: A litigant is a party to a lawsuit, someone who takes or defends a case before the courts.

clue.text: Trick played on relation with seafood

blocks.note: a scam is a swindle or trick
pi is the fixed ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter

explanation.surface: A prank pulled on a family member involving fish and shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relation' suggests a relative, but it is a mathematical ratio; in an across clue 'on' places the first piece before the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are langoustines or Dublin Bay prawns, typically served breaded and fried.

clue.text: See 5
Question of the lost explosive paper in the West Indies

indicators.note: items placed in a region sit within its borders, so the abbreviation wraps around the other pieces

blocks.note: HE is the abbreviation for high explosive
a ream is a quantity of paper, 500 sheets
WI is the abbreviation for the West Indies

explanation.surface: A lost traveller with a bomb and a sheaf of paper somewhere in the Caribbean.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has lost their bearings asks this to discover their location.

clue.text: He was chiefly responsible for the Egyptian assertion of freedom

definitions.text: He was chiefly responsible for the Egyptian assertion of freedom

blocks.note: the letters sit across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A history note on the leader behind Egypt's bid for independence.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no separate indicator: the whole clue describes the man, and his name runs across two of its words.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamal Abdel Nasser led Egypt from 1954, ending British influence and nationalising the Suez Canal in 1956.

clue.text: Emperor with a bit of fruit

blocks.note: a sultan is an Ottoman emperor
taken as written

explanation.surface: An emperor holding a morsel of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit of fruit' looks like a letter-selection signal, but 'a' is a piece and 'bit of fruit' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultana is a dried seedless golden grape, one small piece of dried fruit.

clue.text: Military group with digital bone of tailless marsupial

indicators.note: an animal without a tail has lost its end, so the word drops its final letter

blocks.note: first meaning: the Lebanese Christian party and militia founded in 1936
second meaning: a bone of a finger or toe
an Australasian tree-dwelling marsupial such as a cuscus

explanation.surface: Soldiers carrying a finger bone from a kangaroo-like animal.
explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions and a piece of wordplay share one answer; 'digital' means of the fingers, not of computers.
explanation.definitionFit: A phalanx bone is also called a phalange, and the Lebanese Phalange took its name from the ancient massed infantry formation.

clue.text: Falls back once more on painter

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the word is read from its end

blocks.note: once more means again
RA, Royal Academician, a painter in crossword convention

explanation.surface: An artist tumbling backwards again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falls' reads as a verb, but it is the noun for a waterfall.
explanation.definitionFit: Niagara is the famous group of waterfalls on the border between Canada and New York State.

clue.text: Concealed cupboard

blocks.note: first meaning: secret, hidden from view, as in a secret drinker
second meaning: a small storage room or recess

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means secret or private, and as a noun it means a storage room for clothes or brooms.

clue.text: Concerned with the smallest parts of a beast with copper guard

blocks.note: a mole is a small burrowing animal
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a lar is one of the Lares, Roman household gods who guarded the home

explanation.surface: A tiny animal protected by a policeman as its minder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' invites a policeman, but it is the metal; the Lares were the guardian spirits of a Roman household.
explanation.definitionFit: Molecules are the minute units of a substance, so anything molecular deals with matter at that tiny scale.

clue.text: Fellow -1 down to be amusing

indicators.note: a minus sign means subtract, and with the number one it takes a single letter away

blocks.note: co- as a prefix means fellow, as in co-worker
the last word of the answer to 1 down

explanation.surface: Someone a little down, trying to be funny.
explanation.walkthrough: The minus sign before 1 means one letter is taken off the cross-referenced word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something comic is funny, intended to make people laugh.

clue.text: Not the highest place in Wales?

blocks.note: first meaning: a poetic contraction for underneath, a low position
second meaning: a town in south Wales, near Swansea

explanation.surface: Asking about a Welsh spot that is not a mountain summit.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one description of a lowland Welsh spot, but it splits into a poetic word for below and the town's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh town shares its spelling with the poetic word for below, which describes a lowly position.

clue.text: Personal attraction that works

blocks.note: first meaning: the power of pleasing or delighting people
second meaning: a spell or amulet, something that works magic

explanation.surface: Praising an appealing personality that gets results.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the quality of being delightful to others and a magic spell or talisman believed to have effect.

clue.text: Draw a harlot as a wife?

blocks.note: stale is an archaic word for a prostitute, used by Shakespeare
a mate is a spouse or partner

explanation.surface: An artist told to sketch a prostitute posing as a married woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' looks like an instruction to sketch, but it is the chess result.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess, a position where the side to move has no legal move but is not in check ends the game level.

clue.text: Eyes down and see which pastes act incorrectly

indicators.note: acting incorrectly means behaving wrongly, so the letters are in the wrong order and must be put right

blocks.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: A bingo caller or teacher telling everyone to look down and spot which glues are misbehaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eyes down' is the bingo call to begin; here it simply tells the reader to look below.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase tells people to keep looking in a given spot because news or developments are coming soon.
